reuse.why: The new getExpectedAmount reuses the existing approx tolerance helper getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules and delegates ranged/missing amounts to the existing getScheduledAmount.

duplication.why: No logic is copied; the only cost is a second exported amount function sitting beside getScheduledAmount, so callers now have two entry points for the expected amount.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount and every server and client consumer imports it from there.

scope.why: All expected-amount consumers are switched consistently, but this also changes the figures shown and searched in the schedule list/table cells, which goes a bit beyond planning.

maintainability.why: One small function owns the worst-case rule and callers pass the op explicitly; keeping getScheduledAmount exported alongside (still used by useScheduleEdit) leaves room for future callers to pick the wrong one.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Uses getApproxNumberThreshold and getScheduledAmount rather than recomputing tolerance or range ends.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedAmount wraps getScheduledAmount instead of re-deriving the ranged rule.

one_place.where: getExpectedAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts, used by preview transactions, forecast, schedule templates, schedule actions/posting, the API model, Balance and the schedule list/table components.
